content:
aisha-cs: FYI - Lumina (acct: lumina-prod) onboarding hit brief auth+rate blips during SDK init in staging around 10:02 UTC. Getting a mix of 401 and 429s. Can we triage?

ken-devex: Ack - can you paste the init snippet and the first 10s of logs? Is this browser or server SDK?

aisha-cs: Server-side node, using their standard bootstrap. Snippet:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, concurrency: 8 });
await client.chat.generate(...);
```
Logs (sanitized):
`2026-03-20T10:02:03Z handshake failed: status=401 reason="token_expired"`
`2026-03-20T10:02:04Z rate_limit exceeded: window=60s allowed=120 got=250`
`2026-03-20T10:02:04Z handshake failed: status=429 reason="concurrency_window"`

luca-sre: Quick read: two possibilities — their ephemeral token TTL is very short or their init is massively parallel (warmup stampede). Also seen edge proxies reject slightly skewed nbf/iat claims causing 401s while upstream counts requests for rate windows -> mixed 401/429.

ken-devex: Can you grab one of the tokens (base64 header+payload only, obfuscate sig) so we can see iat/exp/nbf? Also which region?

aisha-cs: Pasted payload (obfuscated): `{"iat":1700506920,"exp":1700506985,"aud":"redwood","sub":"lumina-svc"}` — TTL looks to be ~65s. Region: eu-west-1.

luca-sre: That's very short for server processes that create N parallel connections. If their node process forks or worker pool spins up, multiple simultaneous preflights will be hitting the edge with the same fresh token TTL and then some will be rejected due to minor clock drift or token validation jitter.

ken-devex: Two-pronged mitigation: 1) short-term: bump account rate window and raise concurrency limit for lumina to avoid renewal-risk 2) advise customer to increase token lifetime to >= 5min for server SDKs or add init jitter.

aisha-cs: Lumina says they can't change token TTL easily (their IAM team locked it). Asking if we can do anything server-side.

luca-sre: We can: - add 60s clock-leeway on edge token validation for this account OR - enable soft-accept mode (accept close-exp tokens and log) for canary region. Which do you prefer?

ken-devex: Soft-accept mode sounds safer; no permanent policy change. Can we do a canary for just lumina in eu-west-1?

luca-sre: I can push a canary rule to the edge that allows tokens with up to 60s skew for the lumina tenant. Will open a short-lived rate buffer too.

deploy-bot: deploy started: edge-proxy/canaries/edge-leeway-for-lumina #4578 — queued -> running

aisha-cs: Thanks. Also Lumina is worried about being charged for the retries; they asked if we can temporarily double their rate limit while we stabilize. Renewal risk if this hits prod.

ken-devex: I support doubling for 24h. It buys breathing room while they patch tokens or we roll a client-side jitter.

luca-sre: Done: increased account rate quota to 2x for 24h and enabled 60s leeway in eu-west-1 for lumina. Monitoring dashboards: /orgs/lumina/metrics -> watch 429s and 5xx.

aisha-cs: Lumina confirmed reduced 401s immediately after canary. 429s dropped ~85% after quota bump. They will follow up with their IAM team to lengthen TTL and implement init jitter.

ken-devex: Action items:
- ken-devex: follow up with Lumina engineering to land SDK jitter patch (small randomized 50-500ms stagger) — ETA next deploy
- luca-sre: revert leeway and quota in 24h if stable; keep alerts for spike -> paging
- aisha-cs: update account health notes and renewal tracker (reduce risk if stable)

aisha-cs: Thanks all — marking as monitored. :thumbsup:

luca-sre: quick note for infra: consider adding a server SDK guidance page: "ephemeral token best practices (recommended TTL, init jitter)" — will open a tiny RFC. :memo:
